Resting is a way to hold space for ourselves and is a powerful act of resistance in a society that expects us to keep going, to continue producing, to perpetually give. layer_name: Some people are affected by everything around them. A crowded room leaves them drained. A hard conversation lingers for hours after it's over. Over time, it gets difficult to tell what's actually yours and what you've picked up from everyone and everything around you. If that sounds familiar, here's something worth knowing: protection doesn't mean shutting the world out. Most people think of energetic protection as building walls. Disconnecting. Guarding yourself. But real protection is sovereignty. It's knowing where you end and everything else begins. Staying connected to yourself even when life is loud, demanding, or overwhelming. The question isn't how to keep the world out. It's how you strengthen your connection to what's actually yours. That connection isn't built once. It's rebuilt, again and again, especially on the days the world asks the most of you. Having something tangible to return to makes that easier. This is why I work with crystals the way I do. Each piece is intentionally created and energetically prepared to act as a marker of that line, a physical reminder of where you end and everything else begins. When you're overwhelmed, or pulled in six directions, or carrying something that isn't yours, the piece is there to bring you back to yourself. Worn consistently, it becomes less about protection from the world and more about staying rooted in who you are inside it. The more connected you are to yourself, the less you need to keep it out.

layer_name: There’s something magical about clasping your lucky necklace and letting it fall against your chest before leaving the house. Practices of adornment and rituals of wearing jewelry are time-honored traditions, and the use of ritual jewelry goes back thousands of years. Ancient people have been discovered buried with their sacred jewelry pieces in every culture. In one instance, in a burial mound in southwestern Siberia, archaeologists discovered the glass beads of a necklace believed to be 2,600 years old. Rituals of adornment are not solely for the past, as jewelry can be imbued with spells, worked with in rituals, and called upon for healing in modern life. Perhaps you are already working with jewelry ritually subconsciously, or maybe you are already ritually minded, casting spells with your sacred and favorite pieces.

layer_name: Call on rituals of adornment to help set intentions. To do this, first, cleanse the piece using sacred smoke, salt, or crystals. Then, hold the jewelry in both your hands. Speak your intention over the jewelry three times. For example, “I call in love in all its forms into my life for the highest good,” or “I call in abundance for myself and my community for the highest good.” Remember your intention when you take the jewelry on or off. Or check in daily with the piece as you wear it, reminding yourself to cultivate this intention in your life.

layer_name: Talismans have been around since the Stone Age, and their etymology is from Ancient Greek meaning "completion". They are objects imbued with magical properties intended to guide, empower, and protect their owners. Working with talismans remind us that life itself is a ceremony – personally we love an intentionally selected crystal, a protective pendant, or a luck attracting bracelet.

layer_name: When working with crystals as talismans, one of the most important things is to bring clear intention to your practice. Allow the crystals to guide you and support your intention.

layer_name: Precious metals and gemstones come from the earth, carrying old, old stories. As a mother-led brand we’re in business to treasure these stories, ensuring that future generations can connect with them, and carry them on. All of our products are consciously crafted. Our gold is recycled solid gold, our gemstones are ethically sourced from local tradesmen and support local economies, our diamonds are lab grown, and our sacred smoke tools are sourced from First Nations People and sold with their permission. Your rituals are imbued with the highest intentions, and we believe your tools should be sourced that way, too.

Precious metals and gemstones come from the earth, carrying old, old stories. As a mother-led brand we’re in business to treasure these stories, ensuring that future generations can connect with them, and carry them on.

Your rituals are imbued with the highest intentions, and we believe your tools should be sourced that way, too.
